Uniform and guided GAS: k=3, 5 and 7 for each dataset

Report information and navigation

Ranking across all new variants from both rounds: highest mean balanced accuracy across LDA and SVM, each averaged over 20 seeds. Objectives are compared separately within each dataset, panel size and preparation; no best seed is selected. All nine benchmarks are reported (Plasma, S1 and Shotgun × k=3, 5 and 7), with 18 selected configurations: one uniform and one guided per combination. Original GAS results are references, not candidates in this ranking of new variants.

Retrospective selection of the best observed result across multiple trials, with feature selection preceding LOOCV. This is exploratory, not independent validation or evidence of statistical, clinical or quantum superiority. SD is across seeds. Differences use the same k; QAOA comparisons do not mix panel sizes.

Plots show random, uniform GAS, guided GAS, local QAOA and Bias Field (BF-DCQO), using previously frozen comparator values without new runs. Random and QAOA use the same k as GAS. Bias Field is separated in purple: published k=5 accuracy on the right axis, not verified balanced accuracy. Its k=3/7 values are unreported; the k=5 result is not reassigned to those sizes and no SD is invented.

QUBO and guide equations are typeset from LaTeX using embedded KaTeX, with accessible MathML. This HTML works offline. Original biomarker names are preserved.

Uniform GAS — pearson_mean
Selection summary

Best variant of this preparation at k=3 among 7 new objectives. Mean across LDA/SVM: 86.79%, using all 20 seeds.

QUBO construction

Absolute Pearson correlation between each biomarker and the class label. Redundancy: absolute pairwise Pearson correlation.

Minimize the quadratic energy at fixed cardinality. Relevance is normalized by its maximum. Equivalently, maximize weighted mean relevance minus weighted mean pair redundancy. Canonical coefficients are quantized at the scale shown below.

\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^N} x^\top Qx \quad \mathrm{subject\ to}\quad \sum_{i=1}^N x_i=3,\qquad \alpha=0.77
I_i=\frac{r_i}{\max_j r_j},\quad Q_{ii}=-\frac{\alpha I_i}{k},\quad Q_{ij}=\frac{(1-\alpha)R_{ij}}{k(k-1)}\ (i\ne j)
\max_{|S|=k}\left[\frac{\alpha}{k}\sum_{i\in S}I_i-\frac{1-\alpha}{\binom{k}{2}}\sum_{\substack{i<j\\i,j\in S}}R_{ij}\right]
\mathrm{Coefficient\ scale}=2^{20}

Here r is raw relevance, I is normalized relevance, R is pairwise redundancy, N is the candidate count, and S is a selected panel. Zero maxima yield zero normalized statistics; the implementation guards denominators with a small positive floor.

Preparation guide

Uniform preparation: zero logits and equal probability for every feasible panel. No relevance- or redundancy-based guide is used.

\ell_i=0,\qquad P_{\mathrm{prep}}(S)=\binom{N}{k}^{-1},\quad |S|=k

Ideal GAS: cap=1, 32 rounds, uniform initialization. These probabilities describe preparation before amplification, not the final selected-panel distribution. QUBO and guide statistics use the full cohort before LOOCV.

Guided GAS — pearson_mean
Selection summary

Best variant of this preparation at k=3 among 7 new objectives. Mean across LDA/SVM: 87.02%, using all 20 seeds.

QUBO construction

Absolute Pearson correlation between each biomarker and the class label. Redundancy: absolute pairwise Pearson correlation.

Minimize the quadratic energy at fixed cardinality. Relevance is normalized by its maximum. Equivalently, maximize weighted mean relevance minus weighted mean pair redundancy. Canonical coefficients are quantized at the scale shown below.

\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^N} x^\top Qx \quad \mathrm{subject\ to}\quad \sum_{i=1}^N x_i=3,\qquad \alpha=0.77
I_i=\frac{r_i}{\max_j r_j},\quad Q_{ii}=-\frac{\alpha I_i}{k},\quad Q_{ij}=\frac{(1-\alpha)R_{ij}}{k(k-1)}\ (i\ne j)
\max_{|S|=k}\left[\frac{\alpha}{k}\sum_{i\in S}I_i-\frac{1-\alpha}{\binom{k}{2}}\sum_{\substack{i<j\\i,j\in S}}R_{ij}\right]
\mathrm{Coefficient\ scale}=2^{20}

Here r is raw relevance, I is normalized relevance, R is pairwise redundancy, N is the candidate count, and S is a selected panel. Zero maxima yield zero normalized statistics; the implementation guards denominators with a small positive floor.

Preparation guide

Product guide conditioned on panel size, with fixed strength 4. Redundancy is divided by its maximum, or set to zero if the maximum is zero. The guide uses the relevance from this same objective. Changing the QUBO trade-off does not change guide strength.

\widehat R_{ij}=\frac{R_{ij}}{\max_{a,b}R_{ab}},\qquad \ell_i=\operatorname{clip}\left(4\left[I_i-\frac{1}{N-1}\sum_{j\ne i}\widehat R_{ij}\right],-12,12\right)
P_{\mathrm{prep}}(S)=\frac{\exp\left(\sum_{i\in S}\ell_i\right)}{\sum_{|T|=k}\exp\left(\sum_{j\in T}\ell_j\right)},\quad |S|=k

Ideal GAS: cap=1, 32 rounds, uniform initialization. These probabilities describe preparation before amplification, not the final selected-panel distribution. QUBO and guide statistics use the full cohort before LOOCV.

Uniform GAS — relief5
Selection summary

Best variant of this preparation at k=5 among 7 new objectives. Mean across LDA/SVM: 87.64%, using all 20 seeds.

QUBO construction

Binary ReliefF: features scaled to [0,1], every sample used as an anchor, 5 nearest same-class neighbors and 5 opposite-class neighbors under L1 distance. Relevance is the mean opposite-class minus same-class feature distance, clipped below at zero. Redundancy: absolute pairwise Pearson correlation.

Minimize the quadratic energy at fixed cardinality. Relevance is normalized by its maximum. Equivalently, maximize weighted mean relevance minus weighted mean pair redundancy. Canonical coefficients are quantized at the scale shown below.

\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^N} x^\top Qx \quad \mathrm{subject\ to}\quad \sum_{i=1}^N x_i=5,\qquad \alpha=0.77
I_i=\frac{r_i}{\max_j r_j},\quad Q_{ii}=-\frac{\alpha I_i}{k},\quad Q_{ij}=\frac{(1-\alpha)R_{ij}}{k(k-1)}\ (i\ne j)
\max_{|S|=k}\left[\frac{\alpha}{k}\sum_{i\in S}I_i-\frac{1-\alpha}{\binom{k}{2}}\sum_{\substack{i<j\\i,j\in S}}R_{ij}\right]
\mathrm{Coefficient\ scale}=2^{20}

Here r is raw relevance, I is normalized relevance, R is pairwise redundancy, N is the candidate count, and S is a selected panel. Zero maxima yield zero normalized statistics; the implementation guards denominators with a small positive floor.

Preparation guide

Uniform preparation: zero logits and equal probability for every feasible panel. No relevance- or redundancy-based guide is used.

\ell_i=0,\qquad P_{\mathrm{prep}}(S)=\binom{N}{k}^{-1},\quad |S|=k

Ideal GAS: cap=1, 32 rounds, uniform initialization. These probabilities describe preparation before amplification, not the final selected-panel distribution. QUBO and guide statistics use the full cohort before LOOCV.

Guided GAS — lda_contribution
Selection summary

Best variant of this preparation at k=5 among 7 new objectives. Mean across LDA/SVM: 89.58%, using all 20 seeds.

QUBO construction

Multivariate LDA contribution: standardization followed by lsqr LDA with automatic shrinkage. Relevance is the absolute coefficient times the standardized class-mean difference. Redundancy: absolute pairwise Pearson correlation.

Minimize the quadratic energy at fixed cardinality. Relevance is normalized by its maximum. Equivalently, maximize weighted mean relevance minus weighted mean pair redundancy. Canonical coefficients are quantized at the scale shown below.

\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^N} x^\top Qx \quad \mathrm{subject\ to}\quad \sum_{i=1}^N x_i=5,\qquad \alpha=0.77
I_i=\frac{r_i}{\max_j r_j},\quad Q_{ii}=-\frac{\alpha I_i}{k},\quad Q_{ij}=\frac{(1-\alpha)R_{ij}}{k(k-1)}\ (i\ne j)
\max_{|S|=k}\left[\frac{\alpha}{k}\sum_{i\in S}I_i-\frac{1-\alpha}{\binom{k}{2}}\sum_{\substack{i<j\\i,j\in S}}R_{ij}\right]
\mathrm{Coefficient\ scale}=2^{20}

Here r is raw relevance, I is normalized relevance, R is pairwise redundancy, N is the candidate count, and S is a selected panel. Zero maxima yield zero normalized statistics; the implementation guards denominators with a small positive floor.

Preparation guide

Product guide conditioned on panel size, with fixed strength 4. Redundancy is divided by its maximum, or set to zero if the maximum is zero. The guide uses the relevance from this same objective. Changing the QUBO trade-off does not change guide strength.

\widehat R_{ij}=\frac{R_{ij}}{\max_{a,b}R_{ab}},\qquad \ell_i=\operatorname{clip}\left(4\left[I_i-\frac{1}{N-1}\sum_{j\ne i}\widehat R_{ij}\right],-12,12\right)
P_{\mathrm{prep}}(S)=\frac{\exp\left(\sum_{i\in S}\ell_i\right)}{\sum_{|T|=k}\exp\left(\sum_{j\in T}\ell_j\right)},\quad |S|=k

Ideal GAS: cap=1, 32 rounds, uniform initialization. These probabilities describe preparation before amplification, not the final selected-panel distribution. QUBO and guide statistics use the full cohort before LOOCV.

Uniform GAS — lda_contribution
Selection summary

Best variant of this preparation at k=7 among 7 new objectives. Mean across LDA/SVM: 91.25%, using all 20 seeds.

QUBO construction

Multivariate LDA contribution: standardization followed by lsqr LDA with automatic shrinkage. Relevance is the absolute coefficient times the standardized class-mean difference. Redundancy: absolute pairwise Pearson correlation.

Minimize the quadratic energy at fixed cardinality. Relevance is normalized by its maximum. Equivalently, maximize weighted mean relevance minus weighted mean pair redundancy. Canonical coefficients are quantized at the scale shown below.

\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^N} x^\top Qx \quad \mathrm{subject\ to}\quad \sum_{i=1}^N x_i=7,\qquad \alpha=0.77
I_i=\frac{r_i}{\max_j r_j},\quad Q_{ii}=-\frac{\alpha I_i}{k},\quad Q_{ij}=\frac{(1-\alpha)R_{ij}}{k(k-1)}\ (i\ne j)
\max_{|S|=k}\left[\frac{\alpha}{k}\sum_{i\in S}I_i-\frac{1-\alpha}{\binom{k}{2}}\sum_{\substack{i<j\\i,j\in S}}R_{ij}\right]
\mathrm{Coefficient\ scale}=2^{20}

Here r is raw relevance, I is normalized relevance, R is pairwise redundancy, N is the candidate count, and S is a selected panel. Zero maxima yield zero normalized statistics; the implementation guards denominators with a small positive floor.

Preparation guide

Uniform preparation: zero logits and equal probability for every feasible panel. No relevance- or redundancy-based guide is used.

\ell_i=0,\qquad P_{\mathrm{prep}}(S)=\binom{N}{k}^{-1},\quad |S|=k

Ideal GAS: cap=1, 32 rounds, uniform initialization. These probabilities describe preparation before amplification, not the final selected-panel distribution. QUBO and guide statistics use the full cohort before LOOCV.

Guided GAS — lda_contribution
Selection summary

Best variant of this preparation at k=7 among 7 new objectives. Mean across LDA/SVM: 90.90%, using all 20 seeds.

QUBO construction

Multivariate LDA contribution: standardization followed by lsqr LDA with automatic shrinkage. Relevance is the absolute coefficient times the standardized class-mean difference. Redundancy: absolute pairwise Pearson correlation.

Minimize the quadratic energy at fixed cardinality. Relevance is normalized by its maximum. Equivalently, maximize weighted mean relevance minus weighted mean pair redundancy. Canonical coefficients are quantized at the scale shown below.

\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^N} x^\top Qx \quad \mathrm{subject\ to}\quad \sum_{i=1}^N x_i=7,\qquad \alpha=0.77
I_i=\frac{r_i}{\max_j r_j},\quad Q_{ii}=-\frac{\alpha I_i}{k},\quad Q_{ij}=\frac{(1-\alpha)R_{ij}}{k(k-1)}\ (i\ne j)
\max_{|S|=k}\left[\frac{\alpha}{k}\sum_{i\in S}I_i-\frac{1-\alpha}{\binom{k}{2}}\sum_{\substack{i<j\\i,j\in S}}R_{ij}\right]
\mathrm{Coefficient\ scale}=2^{20}

Here r is raw relevance, I is normalized relevance, R is pairwise redundancy, N is the candidate count, and S is a selected panel. Zero maxima yield zero normalized statistics; the implementation guards denominators with a small positive floor.

Preparation guide

Product guide conditioned on panel size, with fixed strength 4. Redundancy is divided by its maximum, or set to zero if the maximum is zero. The guide uses the relevance from this same objective. Changing the QUBO trade-off does not change guide strength.

\widehat R_{ij}=\frac{R_{ij}}{\max_{a,b}R_{ab}},\qquad \ell_i=\operatorname{clip}\left(4\left[I_i-\frac{1}{N-1}\sum_{j\ne i}\widehat R_{ij}\right],-12,12\right)
P_{\mathrm{prep}}(S)=\frac{\exp\left(\sum_{i\in S}\ell_i\right)}{\sum_{|T|=k}\exp\left(\sum_{j\in T}\ell_j\right)},\quad |S|=k

Ideal GAS: cap=1, 32 rounds, uniform initialization. These probabilities describe preparation before amplification, not the final selected-panel distribution. QUBO and guide statistics use the full cohort before LOOCV.

Guided GAS — fisher_mean
Selection summary

Best variant of this preparation at k=3 among 8 new objectives. Mean across LDA/SVM: 91.78%, using all 20 seeds.

QUBO construction

Univariate Fisher relevance: squared class-mean difference divided by the sum of class variances. Redundancy: absolute pairwise Pearson correlation.

Minimize the quadratic energy at fixed cardinality. Relevance is normalized by its maximum. Equivalently, maximize weighted mean relevance minus weighted mean pair redundancy. Canonical coefficients are quantized at the scale shown below.

\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^N} x^\top Qx \quad \mathrm{subject\ to}\quad \sum_{i=1}^N x_i=3,\qquad \alpha=0.77
I_i=\frac{r_i}{\max_j r_j},\quad Q_{ii}=-\frac{\alpha I_i}{k},\quad Q_{ij}=\frac{(1-\alpha)R_{ij}}{k(k-1)}\ (i\ne j)
\max_{|S|=k}\left[\frac{\alpha}{k}\sum_{i\in S}I_i-\frac{1-\alpha}{\binom{k}{2}}\sum_{\substack{i<j\\i,j\in S}}R_{ij}\right]
\mathrm{Coefficient\ scale}=2^{20}

Here r is raw relevance, I is normalized relevance, R is pairwise redundancy, N is the candidate count, and S is a selected panel. Zero maxima yield zero normalized statistics; the implementation guards denominators with a small positive floor.

Preparation guide

Product guide conditioned on panel size, with fixed strength 4. Redundancy is divided by its maximum, or set to zero if the maximum is zero. The guide uses the relevance from this same objective. Changing the QUBO trade-off does not change guide strength.

\widehat R_{ij}=\frac{R_{ij}}{\max_{a,b}R_{ab}},\qquad \ell_i=\operatorname{clip}\left(4\left[I_i-\frac{1}{N-1}\sum_{j\ne i}\widehat R_{ij}\right],-12,12\right)
P_{\mathrm{prep}}(S)=\frac{\exp\left(\sum_{i\in S}\ell_i\right)}{\sum_{|T|=k}\exp\left(\sum_{j\in T}\ell_j\right)},\quad |S|=k

Ideal GAS: cap=1, 32 rounds, uniform initialization. These probabilities describe preparation before amplification, not the final selected-panel distribution. QUBO and guide statistics use the full cohort before LOOCV.

Guided GAS — relief5
Selection summary

Best variant of this preparation at k=7 among 8 new objectives. Mean across LDA/SVM: 94.55%, using all 20 seeds.

QUBO construction

Binary ReliefF: features scaled to [0,1], every sample used as an anchor, 5 nearest same-class neighbors and 5 opposite-class neighbors under L1 distance. Relevance is the mean opposite-class minus same-class feature distance, clipped below at zero. Redundancy: absolute pairwise Pearson correlation.

Minimize the quadratic energy at fixed cardinality. Relevance is normalized by its maximum. Equivalently, maximize weighted mean relevance minus weighted mean pair redundancy. Canonical coefficients are quantized at the scale shown below.

\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^N} x^\top Qx \quad \mathrm{subject\ to}\quad \sum_{i=1}^N x_i=7,\qquad \alpha=0.77
I_i=\frac{r_i}{\max_j r_j},\quad Q_{ii}=-\frac{\alpha I_i}{k},\quad Q_{ij}=\frac{(1-\alpha)R_{ij}}{k(k-1)}\ (i\ne j)
\max_{|S|=k}\left[\frac{\alpha}{k}\sum_{i\in S}I_i-\frac{1-\alpha}{\binom{k}{2}}\sum_{\substack{i<j\\i,j\in S}}R_{ij}\right]
\mathrm{Coefficient\ scale}=2^{20}

Here r is raw relevance, I is normalized relevance, R is pairwise redundancy, N is the candidate count, and S is a selected panel. Zero maxima yield zero normalized statistics; the implementation guards denominators with a small positive floor.

Preparation guide

Product guide conditioned on panel size, with fixed strength 4. Redundancy is divided by its maximum, or set to zero if the maximum is zero. The guide uses the relevance from this same objective. Changing the QUBO trade-off does not change guide strength.

\widehat R_{ij}=\frac{R_{ij}}{\max_{a,b}R_{ab}},\qquad \ell_i=\operatorname{clip}\left(4\left[I_i-\frac{1}{N-1}\sum_{j\ne i}\widehat R_{ij}\right],-12,12\right)
P_{\mathrm{prep}}(S)=\frac{\exp\left(\sum_{i\in S}\ell_i\right)}{\sum_{|T|=k}\exp\left(\sum_{j\in T}\ell_j\right)},\quad |S|=k

Ideal GAS: cap=1, 32 rounds, uniform initialization. These probabilities describe preparation before amplification, not the final selected-panel distribution. QUBO and guide statistics use the full cohort before LOOCV.

Uniform GAS — pearson_mean
Selection summary

Best variant of this preparation at k=3 among 8 new objectives. Mean across LDA/SVM: 77.69%, using all 20 seeds.

QUBO construction

Absolute Pearson correlation between each biomarker and the class label. Redundancy: absolute pairwise Pearson correlation.

Minimize the quadratic energy at fixed cardinality. Relevance is normalized by its maximum. Equivalently, maximize weighted mean relevance minus weighted mean pair redundancy. Canonical coefficients are quantized at the scale shown below.

\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^N} x^\top Qx \quad \mathrm{subject\ to}\quad \sum_{i=1}^N x_i=3,\qquad \alpha=0.77
I_i=\frac{r_i}{\max_j r_j},\quad Q_{ii}=-\frac{\alpha I_i}{k},\quad Q_{ij}=\frac{(1-\alpha)R_{ij}}{k(k-1)}\ (i\ne j)
\max_{|S|=k}\left[\frac{\alpha}{k}\sum_{i\in S}I_i-\frac{1-\alpha}{\binom{k}{2}}\sum_{\substack{i<j\\i,j\in S}}R_{ij}\right]
\mathrm{Coefficient\ scale}=2^{20}

Here r is raw relevance, I is normalized relevance, R is pairwise redundancy, N is the candidate count, and S is a selected panel. Zero maxima yield zero normalized statistics; the implementation guards denominators with a small positive floor.

Preparation guide

Uniform preparation: zero logits and equal probability for every feasible panel. No relevance- or redundancy-based guide is used.

\ell_i=0,\qquad P_{\mathrm{prep}}(S)=\binom{N}{k}^{-1},\quad |S|=k

Ideal GAS: cap=1, 32 rounds, uniform initialization. These probabilities describe preparation before amplification, not the final selected-panel distribution. QUBO and guide statistics use the full cohort before LOOCV.

Guided GAS — fisher_weak
Selection summary

Best variant of this preparation at k=3 among 8 new objectives. Mean across LDA/SVM: 82.24%, using all 20 seeds.

QUBO construction

Univariate Fisher relevance, with a weak redundancy penalty. Redundancy: absolute pairwise Pearson correlation.

Minimize the quadratic energy at fixed cardinality. Relevance is normalized by its maximum. Equivalently, maximize weighted mean relevance minus weighted mean pair redundancy. Canonical coefficients are quantized at the scale shown below.

\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^N} x^\top Qx \quad \mathrm{subject\ to}\quad \sum_{i=1}^N x_i=3,\qquad \alpha=0.95
I_i=\frac{r_i}{\max_j r_j},\quad Q_{ii}=-\frac{\alpha I_i}{k},\quad Q_{ij}=\frac{(1-\alpha)R_{ij}}{k(k-1)}\ (i\ne j)
\max_{|S|=k}\left[\frac{\alpha}{k}\sum_{i\in S}I_i-\frac{1-\alpha}{\binom{k}{2}}\sum_{\substack{i<j\\i,j\in S}}R_{ij}\right]
\mathrm{Coefficient\ scale}=2^{20}

Here r is raw relevance, I is normalized relevance, R is pairwise redundancy, N is the candidate count, and S is a selected panel. Zero maxima yield zero normalized statistics; the implementation guards denominators with a small positive floor.

Preparation guide

Product guide conditioned on panel size, with fixed strength 4. Redundancy is divided by its maximum, or set to zero if the maximum is zero. The guide uses the relevance from this same objective. Changing the QUBO trade-off does not change guide strength.

\widehat R_{ij}=\frac{R_{ij}}{\max_{a,b}R_{ab}},\qquad \ell_i=\operatorname{clip}\left(4\left[I_i-\frac{1}{N-1}\sum_{j\ne i}\widehat R_{ij}\right],-12,12\right)
P_{\mathrm{prep}}(S)=\frac{\exp\left(\sum_{i\in S}\ell_i\right)}{\sum_{|T|=k}\exp\left(\sum_{j\in T}\ell_j\right)},\quad |S|=k

Ideal GAS: cap=1, 32 rounds, uniform initialization. These probabilities describe preparation before amplification, not the final selected-panel distribution. QUBO and guide statistics use the full cohort before LOOCV.

Uniform GAS — fisher_only
Selection summary

Best variant of this preparation at k=7 among 8 new objectives. Mean across LDA/SVM: 75.94%, using all 20 seeds.

QUBO construction

Univariate Fisher relevance, without a redundancy penalty. No redundancy: the redundancy matrix is zero.

Minimize the quadratic energy at fixed cardinality. Relevance is normalized by its maximum. Equivalently, maximize weighted mean relevance minus weighted mean pair redundancy. Canonical coefficients are quantized at the scale shown below.

\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^N} x^\top Qx \quad \mathrm{subject\ to}\quad \sum_{i=1}^N x_i=7,\qquad \alpha=1
I_i=\frac{r_i}{\max_j r_j},\quad Q_{ii}=-\frac{\alpha I_i}{k},\quad Q_{ij}=\frac{(1-\alpha)R_{ij}}{k(k-1)}\ (i\ne j)
\max_{|S|=k}\left[\frac{\alpha}{k}\sum_{i\in S}I_i-\frac{1-\alpha}{\binom{k}{2}}\sum_{\substack{i<j\\i,j\in S}}R_{ij}\right]
\mathrm{Coefficient\ scale}=2^{20}

Here r is raw relevance, I is normalized relevance, R is pairwise redundancy, N is the candidate count, and S is a selected panel. Zero maxima yield zero normalized statistics; the implementation guards denominators with a small positive floor.

Preparation guide

Uniform preparation: zero logits and equal probability for every feasible panel. No relevance- or redundancy-based guide is used.

\ell_i=0,\qquad P_{\mathrm{prep}}(S)=\binom{N}{k}^{-1},\quad |S|=k

Ideal GAS: cap=1, 32 rounds, uniform initialization. These probabilities describe preparation before amplification, not the final selected-panel distribution. QUBO and guide statistics use the full cohort before LOOCV.

Guided GAS — fisher_only
Selection summary

Best variant of this preparation at k=7 among 8 new objectives. Mean across LDA/SVM: 77.17%, using all 20 seeds.

QUBO construction

Univariate Fisher relevance, without a redundancy penalty. No redundancy: the redundancy matrix is zero.

Minimize the quadratic energy at fixed cardinality. Relevance is normalized by its maximum. Equivalently, maximize weighted mean relevance minus weighted mean pair redundancy. Canonical coefficients are quantized at the scale shown below.

\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^N} x^\top Qx \quad \mathrm{subject\ to}\quad \sum_{i=1}^N x_i=7,\qquad \alpha=1
I_i=\frac{r_i}{\max_j r_j},\quad Q_{ii}=-\frac{\alpha I_i}{k},\quad Q_{ij}=\frac{(1-\alpha)R_{ij}}{k(k-1)}\ (i\ne j)
\max_{|S|=k}\left[\frac{\alpha}{k}\sum_{i\in S}I_i-\frac{1-\alpha}{\binom{k}{2}}\sum_{\substack{i<j\\i,j\in S}}R_{ij}\right]
\mathrm{Coefficient\ scale}=2^{20}

Here r is raw relevance, I is normalized relevance, R is pairwise redundancy, N is the candidate count, and S is a selected panel. Zero maxima yield zero normalized statistics; the implementation guards denominators with a small positive floor.

Preparation guide

Product guide conditioned on panel size, with fixed strength 4. Redundancy is divided by its maximum, or set to zero if the maximum is zero. The guide uses the relevance from this same objective. Changing the QUBO trade-off does not change guide strength.

\widehat R_{ij}=\frac{R_{ij}}{\max_{a,b}R_{ab}},\qquad \ell_i=\operatorname{clip}\left(4\left[I_i-\frac{1}{N-1}\sum_{j\ne i}\widehat R_{ij}\right],-12,12\right)
P_{\mathrm{prep}}(S)=\frac{\exp\left(\sum_{i\in S}\ell_i\right)}{\sum_{|T|=k}\exp\left(\sum_{j\in T}\ell_j\right)},\quad |S|=k

Ideal GAS: cap=1, 32 rounds, uniform initialization. These probabilities describe preparation before amplification, not the final selected-panel distribution. QUBO and guide statistics use the full cohort before LOOCV.
